description: The image is labelled as rust / corrosion on a stockbridge damper. In visual terms, orange-brown surface corrosion is expected around exposed metallic edges, bolt holes, pins, or clamp interfaces. The most relevant inspection area is on the clamp, messenger wire, bolts, and counterweight fittings. This is a defect because load-bearing fittings are expected to retain protective galvanizing and adequate section thickness; corrosion indicates coating loss and possible pitting. The observation is inconsistent with the intended function of this component. The component normally attenuates conductor vibration using counterweights connected by a messenger cable near the suspension point, and this condition should be assessed against the design and inspection intent of IEC 61284, IEEE C2 (NESC), ABNT NBR 5422. If left uncorrected, continued corrosion can reduce mechanical strength, seize pins, accelerate fatigue cracking, and ultimately contribute to hardware fracture or conductor drop. Recommended action: schedule close inspection and replacement or refurbishment of the affected hardware; escalate if pitting, section loss, or loose pins are confirmed Severity: moderate.

description: The image is labelled as rust / corrosion on a glass insulator big shackle. description: The image is labelled as rust / corrosion on a yoke suspension. The most relevant inspection area is on the suspension links, shackle, pins, and crossarm attachment points. This is a defect because load-bearing fittings are expected to retain protective galvanizing and adequate section thickness; corrosion indicates coating loss and possible pitting. The observation is inconsistent with the intended function of this component. Recommended action: schedule close inspection and replacement or refurbishment of the affected hardware; escalate if pitting, section loss, or loose pins are confirmed Severity: moderate.
